• U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit Colombia, Peru and Ecuador amid talk in Washington of a rightward regional shift.
• New scrutiny surfaced around alleged Saudi links to 9/11 and how U.S. agencies handled evidence, while analysts reflected on how post-9/11 wars reshaped Russia and China’s ambitions.
Why it matters: Europe’s political center is under strain, diplomacy around the Ukraine war is testing new channels, and Balkan politics and U.S.-Latin America ties reflect shifting alliances with wide implications for regional stability.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text: Populist, far-right, anti-immigration AfD wins vote in eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. Plus, 50 years since The Muppet Show first hit our screensDon’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up hereGood morning. A far-right leader who has won an important state election in Germany has thanked Elon Musk for his support, as voices in Europe warn the result is a serious moment for the continent. No far-right party has led or formed a government in Germany since the defeat of nazism at the end of the second world war.Ulrich Siegmund, the Alternative für Deutschland’s lead candidate, thanked Musk on X after the tech billionaire said “Well done!” in German to the AfD co-founder Alice Weidel. The populist, far-right, anti-immigration party won the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.Will the AfD be able to form a state government? Despite its resounding victory, the party fell just short of a majority. It was seeking an absolute majority in the state legislature to govern alone and overcome the so-called “firewall” of the mainstream parties, which refuse to work with it. The final results showed the AfD falling three seats short, with 39 lawmakers in an 83-member legislature.What has been the reaction in Washington and Moscow? Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the election projection without comment on his Truth Social site. The Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev took a screengrab of Trump’s post and praised a “historic win for the pragmatic AfD”. The AfD is pro-Kremlin, urging a stop to support for Ukraine and pushing for Ukrainians in Germany to no longer receive refugee status.Who else has been saying Trump’s war may not achieve its aims? The US energy secretary, Chris Wright, said on Sunday morning Washington might not be able to reach an agreement with Tehran that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons. “We are strangling their economy to try to bring either a change in policy from the existing regime or a new regime,” he said. Society & Human Rights.title: Rescuers look for survivors after New Delhi hostel collapse kills 7
Society & Human Rights.text:
Rescue workers continue to search for people trapped under the debris of a collapsed building in New Delhi, India, Monday, Sept. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Manish Swarup)2026-09-07T05:44:49Z
                                        NEW DELHI (AP) — Search and rescue teams combed through the debris of a collapsed building in New Delhi on Monday as the death toll climbed to seven, officials said.The five-story building, which housed a boys’ hostel, collapsed on Sunday in Satya Niketan, a densely populated neighborhood known for its private student accommodations near a Delhi University campus.Police, firefighters and crews from India’s disaster response agency continued their search for a second day as earthmovers cleared debris and sniffer dogs worked the site to help rescuers reach those still trapped inside.Rescue crews pulled at least 12 people from under the rubble, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta told reporters at the site on Monday. About 80% of the debris had been cleared and only rubble from the basement remained, she said, adding that six people died and six others were injured in the incident.
    
        
    

Later Monday, rescuers recovered a body, raising the death toll to seven, officials said.According to residents, the building was at least 55 years old and had been under renovation for months before reopening to tenants, mostly students, in August despite work remaining unfinished. Prakash Chand, a resident, said laborers were in the basement carrying out digging work when the building collapsed.

Preliminary findings suggest water accumulation in the basement and ongoing repair work on the aging building may have caused the collapse, Gupta said. She said the government will draft a policy requiring periodic structural audits and safety certificates for buildings used by the public, including student accommodations, nursing homes and schools. “No public activity will be permitted” in buildings that fail to comply, Gupta said.

Society & Human Rights.title: Iranian soccer players who sought asylum in Australia say anthem silence was protest against Tehran
Society & Human Rights.text:
Fatemeh Pasandideh, left, and Atefeh Ramezanisadeh, right, former members of the Iranian women's soccer team, stand with Australia's Minister for Home Affairs, Tony Burke, after receiving their citizenship in Brisbane, Australia, on Aug. 5, 2026. (Department of Home Affairs via AP, File)2026-09-07T06:23:16Z
                                        MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — Two members of the Iranian women’s soccer team who claimed asylum in Australia have confirmed their pivotal refusal to sing the national anthem during the Women’s Asian Cup in March was a protest against Tehran.The first media interview with Atefeh Ramezanisadeh, 34, and Fatemeh Pasandideh, 22, since they abandoned their team to become refugees was broadcast Sunday on Australia’s “60 Minutes” current affairs program.“We just wanted to stand with our people. I was scared at times, but I just tried to do what was right and say that no one should be killed just for protesting,” Ramezanisadeh told Nine Network through an interpreter.The team was criticized in Iran and branded as traitors in the media there for remaining silent when the Iranian national anthem was played ahead of their opening loss against South Korea on March 2.
    
        
    

Some saw it as an act of resistance, while others interpreted it as a show of mourning following the U.S. and Israeli attacks on their homeland which began on Feb. 28. The team offered no public explanation.The gesture led to demonstrators demanding the team be offered asylum in Australia before leaving Sydney on March 10.Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh said they were protesting Tehran’s brutal crackdown on nationwide demonstrations against Iran’s theocratic rule.


    
        




    


Ramezanisadeh said her silence “could have meant any form of torture” for her. “But at that moment, the only thing that gave me peace and a clear conscience was not singing it. I wanted to sing the anthem with pride and from my heart. But because of the situation in Iran, I really couldn’t do it,” she said.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
Pasandideh said through an interpreter of her own silence: “My people put their lives on the line and they were killed. Doing that was the absolute least we could do for them.”Australian Immigration Minister Tony Burke said none of the team had been offered asylum at that time.“At that point, they had absolutely no information from us about the possibility of being able to stay,” Burke said.
    
        
    

“The silence of itself was deeply significant,” he said. “The reaction was the volcanic moment.”

They both now play for the Wynnum Wolves semi-professional soccer team in the city of Brisbane and were made Australian citizens in August.Ramezanisadeh said her parents had asked her to return under the instructions of Iranian authorities.“They tried to reassure me, saying: ‘Nothing will happen to you. Then I will go back and see my family,” she added.

Society & Human Rights.title: How international supermarkets can break up a dinner rut without costing a fortune
Society & Human Rights.text:
Palina Louangketh shops at Idaho Capital Asian Market in Boise, Idaho, on June 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Boone)2026-08-29T05:46:03Z
                                        BOISE, Idaho (AP) — When kitchen burnout hits, figuring out what to make for dinner every day can feel like an impossible task. Eating out or relying on convenience foods are increasingly difficult solutions for many American families, who are facing the biggest jump in grocery prices in a half century. It can also be healthier to cook at home, where it is easier to control things like how much salt or sugar is added to a meal.But in many cities, there’s another way to break the “what’s for dinner” rut without breaking the bank: shopping at international food markets.It can be surprisingly simple to incorporate new flavors into home meals by pairing unfamiliar ingredients with pantry staples, says Palina Louangketh, a self-described foodie and the director of the Idaho Museum of International Diaspora. She also teaches cooking classes, partnering with Boise-area refugees who demonstrate dishes and techniques from their home countries.
    
    This article is part of AP’s Be Well coverage, focusing on wellness, fitness, diet and mental health. Read more Be Well.
    

“Coming here to an international market, you get both a dose of cultural experience but also healthy, fresh exotic ingredients,” Louangketh said on a recent trip to the Idaho Capital Asian Market in Boise, pointing to products from China, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, South Korea and elsewhere. “It doesn’t have to be so scary or unique. If you pair your protein with vegetables and with a starch and add savoriness to it — soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin sauce — you’re covered,” she said.
    
        
    

Yes, navigating a grocery store full of new-to-you products with foreign-language labels might feel daunting at first, said Beryl Shereshewsky, a New York video producer whose YouTube channel is dedicated to exploring dishes and cultural connections from around the world. 


    
        



    


But there are ways to incorporate international supermarkets into your home cooking routine, she said.Here are some tips:
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
Venture outside your neighborhood“I think you would be surprised by how many international markets exist even in small towns and cities,” said Shereshewsky. “Everywhere you go in America, you’re going to find immigrants, and those immigrants are still cooking their foods from their countries and cultures.”Sales at international supermarkets and small grocery stores across the U.S. have been growing steadily for years, according to market research firm IBISWorld.
    
        
    

There are more than 20 international markets in Boise, which has just over 235,000 residents. Several more are located in nearby Meridian, Nampa and Caldwell.People tend to shop near home, Shereshewsky said, but exploring new territory can reveal hidden gems. “It allows you to interact with your city or town in a different way,” she said.

Or a basic side salad can be replaced with Chinese spinach salad, an addictive appetizer made using blanched Taiwanese spinach, vinegary dressing and peanuts. The Taiwanese variety is sweeter and crunchier than the flat-leaf spinach found in most big-box grocery stores.

Society & Human Rights.title: Jamaica takes its case for reparations for Britain’s role in slavery to King Charles III
Society & Human Rights.text:
Jamaica's Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, Olivia Grange, attends a service, in London, Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Alberto Pezzali)2026-09-07T08:33:47Z
                                        LONDON (AP) — Jamaica is taking its campaign for Britain to pay reparations for the ravages of the trans-Atlantic slave trade to King Charles III.Using legal traditions that stretch back to the early days of the British Empire, Jamaica will on Monday petition the king to refer a series of questions about slavery and the U.K.’s responsibility to pay damages to a committee of the Privy Council, which serves as the highest court for former colonies that retain ties to the British legal system.While the petition is formally addressed to the king, Charles has no personal say on whether it will be referred to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, and he will act on the advice of the government. The filing was timed to coincide with the anniversary of the day in 1781 when the Liverpool-registered ship Zong set sail from West Africa with 442 enslaved Africans on board. When water supplies ran low on the way to Jamaica, the crew decided to throw 132 men, women and children overboard, calculating that it would be more profitable to file an insurance claim for the lost “property” than to sell their weakened and dehydrated captives for a reduced price.
    
        
    

The massacre helped speed the abolition of slavery but it wasn’t quickPublicity about the Zong massacre helped fuel the campaign to end slavery in the British Empire. Britain abolished the slave trade in 1807, but it wasn’t until Aug. 1, 1834, that the enslavement of human beings was outlawed.“In relation to the wrongs that were done, we want answers,” Jamaican Culture Minister Olivia Grange told The Associated Press on Sunday before a church service in south London, the first in a series of events scheduled around the filing.


    
        




    


“Once we get those answers, then our attorneys, our lawyers, will determine what the next move is,” she added.Jamaica is a leader of the effort to get Britain and other European nations to apologize for their role in the trans-Atlantic slave trade and pay reparations, both for the enslavement of individuals and for the continuing impact on their descendants around the world. Jamaica said the Caribbean Community, which includes 23 states from the Bahamas to Guyana, endorsed the petition.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
The king has spoken out on the wrongs of slaveryAlthough he has stopped short of endorsing reparations, the king has repeatedly expressed his personal commitment to addressing the historic wrongs of slavery. In a 2024 speech to leaders of the Commonwealth, the voluntary association of countries that succeeded the British Empire, Charles said that the “most painful aspects of our past continue to resonate.”
    
        
    

“None of us can change the past,” he added. “But we can commit, with all our hearts, to learning its lessons and to finding creative ways to right inequalities that endure.”

Buckingham Palace said Monday that it has been working closely with the governor-general of Jamaica, the king’s representative on the island who is appointed on the advice of the Jamaican government, to ensure the petition is “properly lodged.’' While acknowledging that slavery was “abhorrent,” the British government has so far rejected demands for either an apology or reparations.When the United Nations General Assembly in March passed a resolution endorsing reparations as a “concrete step” toward addressing the wrongs of slavery, the U.K. abstained. That was partly because the U.K. believes in the internationally recognized legal concept that the law governing any event is the law of the relevant time, British representative James Kariuki told the U.N.“There is equally no duty to provide reparation for historical acts that were not, at the time those acts were committed, violations of international law,” he said.
    
        
    

Jamaica is taking a political campaign to the courtsJamaica’s petition is an effort to expand the political campaign for reparations into the legal realm, Grange said.The petition asks the Judicial Committee to rule on three questions:— Was the forced transport of African people to Jamaica and their subsequent enslavement illegal because it was contrary to English common law?— Were the forced transport and enslavement of African people crimes against humanity for which the U.K. bears responsibility?— Does the U.K. have an obligation to “provide a remedy” to the people of Jamaica for the forced transport and enslavement of their ancestors?
    
        
    

The procedure could boost support for a Jamaican republic even if rejectedCraig Prescott, an expert on constitutional law and the monarchy at Royal Holloway, University of London, said the move was “quite clever” because it seeks to use an obscure constitutional procedure to address one of the biggest issues in Jamaican society.The right of British people to petition the crown with grievances about the administration of justice stretches back to the Norman conquest of England in 1066, when the king was considered the “fountain of justice throughout his Dominions,” the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council says on its website.Jamaica’s petition is based on an 1833 law that made the committee the highest court for civil and criminal appeals in the British Empire. When the Empire became the Commonwealth of independent nations after World War II, the committee retained that role for the countries that maintain their legal ties to the U.K.Prescott expects the petition to be referred to the Judicial Committee, where a panel of U.K. Supreme Court justices will review it and make a ruling.
    
        
    

But, he said, the justices are usually very cautious about granting such petitions because they sidestep standard legal procedures.“I think, at the very least, the board will look at this with a skeptical eye, not because of questions of whether slavery is wrong or right or otherwise, but just this is a very peculiar legal procedure that is sort of just one on the statute books that rears its head from time to time.”But rejection of the petition could still be a win for Jamaica.Prime Minister Andrew Holness has announced plans to sever ties with the British crown and transform his country into a republic.“It does raise the question of why have a head of state who really does not share the positions that are widely held in Jamaica,” Prescott said. “If those residual links (to Britain) don’t deliver an answer that is what they’re looking for in Jamaica, then you might be looking at severing those links.”___Associated Press journalist Kwiyeon Ha contributed to this report.

Society & Human Rights.title: A Philippine lawmaker charged with corruption in flood control projects
Society & Human Rights.text:
House Speaker Martin Romualdez hears the decision of members of Congress to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte at the House of Representatives in Quezon City in Manila, Philippines, Wednesday, Feb.5, 2025. (AP Photo/Gerard Carreon, File)2026-09-07T09:18:41Z
                                        MANILA, Philippines (AP) — A Philippine lawmaker and former speaker of the House of Representatives was charged Monday for allegedly pocketing millions of dollars in kickbacks from flood control projects in a widening scandal concerning vital public construction to shield communities from typhoons. Rep. Martin Romualdez, a cousin and former political ally of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and others are facing plunder charges at the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan. “The amount involved here is 7.4 billion pesos ($118 million), and this has been divided in various transactions where the money was used,” Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, whose office filed the charges, told a news conference. Romualdez has earlier denied any wrongdoing. Nearly 10,000 flood control projects worth more than 545 billion pesos ($9 billion) that were supposed to have been undertaken since Marcos took office in mid-2022 have come under scrutiny. Many were found to be substandard, overpriced or not built at all.
    
        
    

The Philippines is among the countries most exposed to destructive typhoons, some 20 of which lash the archipelago every year, causing considerable damage and casualties due to floods and landslides. Romualdez, former Rep. Zaldy Co, who used to head the House appropriations committee and is now considered a fugitive after fleeing to Europe, are among several powerful legislators accused of pocketing huge kickbacks. An incumbent senator, a former senator and several ex-government engineers and public works officials as well as wealthy construction executives have been detained while facing trial on corruption charges.


    
        




    


Remulla said so much money was stolen that they tried to hide it by buying several houses, and even donating $1 million to Harvard University.

“This is the just the start,” he said, adding more cases will be filed against Romualdez and others, including plunder and money laundering charges.Marcos has described the alleged scale of corruption as “horrible” and has established an independent commission to investigate. Presidential spokesperson Claire Castro on Monday quoted Marcos as saying earlier that he would not spare even relatives.

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Body of war criminal Mladic lies in state in Serbian capital ahead of funeral
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
A man touches the cross as Serbian national military servicemen stand around the coffin of the former Bosnian Serb army commander Ratko Mladic, who died last week while serving a life sentence for genocide and other atrocities during the war in Bosnia, at the St. Luka Church, in Belgrade, Serbia, Monday, Sept. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Marko Drobnjakovic)2026-09-07T07:19:05Z
                                        BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — The body of Ratko Mladic, the Bosnian Serb commander who died while serving a life sentence for war crimes, lay in state on Monday as Serbia defied European Union warnings against allowing public homage to the man found guilty of the continent’s first case of genocide since World War II.Thousands of mourners arrived early at the small Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Luke in Belgrade to honor Mladic, who is still viewed as a hero by many Serbs. His military officer’s cap and saber rested on the coffin, which was flanked by men in fatigues.The head of the Serbian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Porfirije, led the funeral service while pro-government media in Serbia reported that Mladic will receive full military honors at the burial site. Bosnian Serb nationalist leader Milorad Dodik and the Russian ambassador in Serbia, Alexander Botsan-Kharchenko, were among those present at the funeral.Mladic died at 84 on Aug. 27 in The Hague, Netherlands, where he was serving a life sentence. He was sentenced in 2017 for orchestrating the massacre of more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica in 1995; the yearslong siege of the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo; and other war crimes, including setting up concentration camps for detained non-Serb civilians and enemy soldiers.Since Mladic died, his nationalist admirers have held vigils, painted a series of murals with his image in Belgrade and lit flares in his honor. On Sunday evening, soccer fans displayed a huge image of Mladic and chanted his name at a match in Belgrade. 
    
        
    

Mothers of Srebrenica: It’s a shame!In Bosnia, the Mothers of Srebrenica group that gathers relatives of the victims urged EU reaction, saying that Mladic’s funeral “threatens to become the biggest fascist gathering in Europe in the last 70 years.”“The glorification of genocide is not honor, it’s a shame,” they said on X. A U.N. “safe haven” for Bosniaks (Bosnian Muslims), Srebrenica ended up being overrun by Serbs who forced men and boys to strip, killed them and bulldozed their bodies into mass graves. 


    
        




    


The EU’s foreign service said in a statement that “any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism contradict the most fundamental European values and have no place in the EU or in EU candidate countries.”“We are standing in solidarity with all victims, survivors and their families who suffered from war crimes in countries of former Yugoslavia,” the statement said. Mladic “was a man who gave everything in his life for the Serbian people,” said Milan Dobric, a mourner who traveled from Kosovo for the funeral. “I am glad that this morning people are coming to pay special respect.”
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
Serbian president says gathering is reaction to Western pressureWhile the funeral arrangements were formally made by Mladic’s family, the Serbian government sent a plane last week to bring his remains to Belgrade, and soldiers carried his coffin wrapped in the national flag. A military commemoration was held Saturday at an official Serbian army venue. Populist President Aleksandar Vucic, a former extreme nationalist who supported Serbia’s expansionist policies during the war, described the funeral as an “emotional outpouring” that “has nothing to do” with whether the Serbian government approved it or not. 
    
        
    

Serbia is a candidate nation for European Union membership and has faced strong criticism for honoring Mladic after his death.Marta Kos, the enlargement commissioner for the bloc, canceled an upcoming visit to Serbia in protest, arguing that “the glorification surrounding his death is incompatible with the values on which the EU path is built.”

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Israeli airstrikes on a village in southern Lebanon kill 9 people, wound 13
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
Rescue workers search for victims under the rubble of a building destroyed in an Israeli airstrike in the southern village of Kfar Rumman, Lebanon, Monday, Sept. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Mohammed Zaatari)2026-09-07T08:20:07Z
                                        KFAR RUMMAN, Lebanon (AP) — Israel’s air force carried out two airstrikes early Monday on a southern Lebanese village, killing at least nine people and wounding others, including women and children, Lebanon’s Health Ministry said.Monday’s strikes came amid a new round of escalation between Israel and the militant Hezbollah group despite a truce reached more than two months ago. The strikes also came days after Israel’s military said it is in “operational control” of the strategic Ali Taher hill that overlooks several villages as well as main roads leading to the city of Nabatiyeh.The Health Ministry said one of the strikes hit a building, killing eight people including a child and two women. It added that 11 people were also wounded, including four children and two women.The ministry said that another strike on a car in the village killed a paramedic with the Lebanese Islamic Risala Scout Association and wounded two others.
    
        
    

“We have been living in constant anxiety amid shelling on the outskirts,” said Kfar Rumman resident Fouad Chakaron as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they struck the heart of the town.”Another resident, Saleh Medlej, pointed to the destroyed building and said this was home to families with children. “Are there missiles here?” he asked in reference to the building where the families lived.


    
        




    


“I will not leave this place,” Medlej said, vowing to stay in his hometown despite the airstrikes and shelling.Earlier Monday, Israel’s military issued an evacuation warning for a home in the village of Deir al-Zahrani and shortly afterward a building was struck. The Israeli military said the strike was in retaliation for a drone attack by Hezbollah militants. There was no word on casualties.

On Sunday, Israeli strikes killed at least seven people in southern Lebanon and leveled an empty hospital.A U.S.-brokered truce between Israel and Hezbollah as been repeatedly violated with Israel carrying out airstrikes in Lebanon and Hezbollah firing drones at Israeli troops.Lebanon and Israel in June signed a U.S.-mediated framework deal under which Israeli forces were to withdraw from southern Lebanon in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah, but little progress has been made in its implementation.
    
        
    

Hezbollah is not a party to the Lebanon-Israel talks and has said it will not give up its weapons in any area north of southern Lebanon’s Litani River. Israeli officials, meanwhile, have said they will not withdraw unless Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country.

Climate & Environment.title: Indonesia keeps several airports closed though volcanic eruption is easing
Climate & Environment.text:
People wait as flights are disrupted due to the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Indonesia, Monday, Sept. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana)2026-09-07T06:10:36Z
                                        JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Indonesia kept several airports closed and shifted schools to remote learning Monday though the volcanic eruption that has halted 2,300 flights and coated areas with ash was subsiding.The continuous, 25-hour eruption of Anak Krakatau that produced a fountain of lava and a boom heard 700 kilometers (435 miles) away ended Sunday, the country’s Geological Agency said. But it remained active Monday with moderate, intermittent eruptions, dark ash emissions and small, localized earthquakes, the agency said in a statement. Weather was obscuring visual observations of the eruption.AirNav Indonesia said tests showed volcanic ash present in the airspace around Jakarta and several other cities, prompting authorities to close seven airports until 6 p.m. Monday, while Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, a city in South Sumatra province, resumed normal operations Monday morning.
    
        
    

The closure of four commercial airports managed by state-owned operator InJourney Airports: Jakarta’s international airports of Soekarno-Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma, Husein Sastranegara in West Java’s Bandung city and Radin Inten in Lampung on the southern tip of Sumatra, has disrupted about 2,300 flights and affected 270,337 passengers, according to Indonesia’s Transportation Ministry.The eruption’s impact extended beyond air travel. The government authorized schools in areas affected by volcanic ash, including in Jakarta, West Java, Banten and Lampung provinces, to temporarily move to online learning at home to reduce students’ exposure to ash.


    
        




    


“The probability of additional eruptions in the coming days remains high,” said Lana Saria, head of the Geology Agency. “The main hazards include volcanic bombs, heavy ashfall and possible lava flows if sustained eruptive activity resumes,” she said.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait between Indonesia’s main Java and Sumatra islands. Its name means “child of Krakatau,” and the volcano is the offspring of the infamous Krakatau, whose monumental 1883 eruption triggered a period of global cooling. An eruption of Anak Krakatau in 2018 caused a tsunami that killed at least 430 people in Sumatra and Java. Researchers believe volcanic activity triggered an underwater landslide and caused a large chunk of Anak Krakatau’s southwest slope to collapse and displace a large volume of water. 
    
        
    

Indonesia has more than 120 active volcanoes and frequently experiences eruptions due to its location along the Pacific “Ring of Fire,” the ring of seismic faults around the Pacific Ocean where most global seismic activity occurs.

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli Wins His Home Italian Grand Prix, the First Italian Victor at Monza in 60 Years
Sports.text: SummaryKimi Antonelli started the Italian Grand Prix 19th after taking new power unit components, then charged through the field to win on home soil at MonzaHis victory made him the first Italian driver to win the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966The result marked his seventh win of the season and moved him 66 points clear of teammate George Russell in the drivers' standingsKimi Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid, completing one of the great modern comeback drives on home soil at Monza. The Mercedes driver reeled in and passed teammate and title rival George Russell in the closing laps of the 53-lap race, becoming the first Italian to win his home Grand Prix in six decades.A first win at Monza had looked improbable for Antonelli before the race, with a grid penalty for new power unit components leaving him 19th while Russell lined up near the front. The tone shifted early when Charles Leclerc crashed heavily at the final corner on the second lap, bringing out a red flag. By that point Antonelli had already climbed to 12th, and he sliced through the order at the restart to put himself in contention for the lead.The decisive strategic moment came later, when a mid-race Virtual Safety Car allowed Mercedes to bring Antonelli into the pits for fresher rubber while Russell stayed out. Russell's tyres faded over the closing laps, and Antonelli used his pace advantage to hunt his teammate down. The chase nearly ended in disaster when the pair almost touched at the first chicane and Antonelli ran across the gravel, but he gathered it up and completed the move on the run to Ascari with four laps left."Unbelievable, I'm so happy and I could never have imagined to be here today but we managed to pull it off and I'm really happy," Antonelli said immediately after the race, adding that it felt like "a dream coming true." He also recounted the near miss that almost cost him the win, saying, "I thought I could still do the corner but once I went over a bit of gravel I went straight, and I was like maybe I've lost my chance, but then luckily we still had the pace and managed to bring it home."The historical weight of the result is considerable. No Italian driver had won the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966, a 60-year drought Antonelli ended in front of his home crowd. His starting position added another layer to the achievement, standing as the second-lowest grid slot from which any Grand Prix has been won in Formula 1 history.Behind the leading Mercedes pair, Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the podium after a determined run threaded with bold overtakes. Lando Norris edged McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri for fourth, while Lewis Hamilton led Ferrari home in sixth after Leclerc's early exit, and pole-sitter Pierre Gasly slid back to seventh once the frontrunners cleared off.The championship math is where the day resonates loudest. Antonelli's seventh victory of the season pushed him 66 points clear of Russell in the drivers' standings, converting a back-of-the-grid setback into a commanding statement about who controls the 2026 title fight.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Science & Technology.title: Scientists investigate if a herpes virus is behind the mass deaths of sardines off South Africa
Science & Technology.text:
A catch of sardines pictured at the Hout Bay Harbour near Cape Town, South Africa, on Nov 20, 2011. (AP Photo/Schalk van Zuydam, File)2026-08-29T10:44:33Z
                                        JOHANNESBURG (AP) — Scientists in South Africa are investigating why masses of sardines have washed up dead or dying along parts of the country’s west and south coast — and if a herpes virus detected in the fish is responsible.The mass mortality of sardines this month has so far stumped the country’s Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, though scientists have come to at least one conclusion: it is the first time that the virus in question — pilchard herpesvirus, or PHV — has been identified in sardines off South Africa.PHV, which was linked to two mass sardine mortality events in Australia in the 1990s, can cause inflammation and thickening of sardines’ gills, which interferes with their oxygen uptake, according to the South African environment department.Sardines and pilchards are the same type of fish, with sardines being the younger, smaller ones.
    
        
    

PHV is a fish virus and poses no known risk to human health, the department said, and its detection does not mean that healthy sardines caught commercially or canned sardine products are unsafe to eat.Dozens of sardines taken from affected areas, some dead and some alive, are being examined by scientists at the South African Institute for Aquatic Biodiversity and a local university. In some initial results, dead fish collected from the mass mortality events showed consistently high levels of PHV, the department said in a statement, while live fish that were examined had varied levels of the virus.


    
        




    


Scientists have also considered whether harmful algae found in the ocean or unusually cold sea temperatures or low oxygen conditions might be responsible for the sardine deaths, but “the evidence increasingly points to PHV as the leading explanation,” the environment department said.

Dalene Vosloo, a biological sciences lecturer at South Africa’s University of KwaZulu-Natal who is not involved in the investigation, said the herpes virus may not tell the whole story and “it remains possible that multiple factors contributed to the mortality event.” Changes in water quality or temperature can make fish more vulnerable to disease, she said.
    
        
    

While the investigation continues, the sardine deaths have caused other complications.

These cells, known as peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), are widely used to study infections, autoimmune disorders, cancer and the immune system's response to treatment. Scientists typically identify these cells using fluorescent labels that attach to specific surface markers. While effective, those methods provide limited information about how the cells are functioning and can alter the cells during preparation. As reported in Biophotonics Discovery, a recent study shows how advanced optical imaging can reveal a previously inaccessible layer of information: the metabolic activity of individual immune cells within a complex blood sample.

Health & Pandemic.title: The Italian State Police Just Got a 907 HP Lamborghini Temerario Built for Emergency Organ Deliveries
Health & Pandemic.text: SummaryLamborghini unveiled a specialized 907-hp hybrid vehicle designed specifically for the Italian State PoliceThe high-performance patrol car will be deployed to transport critical medical supplies and organs during emergenciesThe model continues a two-decade initiative that has successfully delivered over 200 organs since launching in 2004When emergency medical runs demand hypercar-level urgency, law enforcement officers now have a new ultimate responder in their arsenal. Lamborghini has officially introduced the Lamborghini Temerario Polizia, a highly customized, high-performance vehicle created specifically for the Italian State Police. The Italian State Police will use the vehicle, which was engineered to conquer the relentless pressure of time-sensitive operations, exclusively to transport organs and critical medical supplies in high-stakes emergencies. To ensure these vital deliveries reach their destinations before time out, the specialized patrol car relies on staggering performance metrics. Pushing the limits of high-speed response, the Temerario Polizia can accelerate from 0-62 mph (0-100 km/h) in a blistering 2.7 seconds. The vehicle ultimately reaches a maximum top speed of 213 mph (343 km/h), transforming open stretches of highway into high-velocity medical corridors.That blistering pace is generated by a radically advanced plug-in hybrid powertrain engineered for maximum forward thrust. At the core of the vehicle sits a heavily armed twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 engine, which operates in seamless tandem with three electric motors to lay down massive power. This complex hybrid setup utilizes an aggressive eight-speed dual-clutch transmission, routing energy alongside a 3.8 kWh battery pack. Such performance metrics elevate the technical capabilities available to modern law enforcement. Combining these components, the advanced system delivers a devastating combined output of 907 hp (677 kW / 920 PS). Adding to that sheer aggressive force, the car produces an equally massive 538 lb-ft (730 Nm) of torque, guaranteeing that the vehicle maintains relentless pace when carrying life-saving cargo.Visually, the vehicle seamlessly merges exotic automotive design with authoritative official duty. The car features a striking blue and white exterior livery, broadcasting its official status with bold "Polizia" badging positioned prominently on the doors. Officials further equipped the exterior with a functional roof-mounted light bar to clear traffic during intense runs. Tri-color graphics inspired directly by the Italian flag accent the exterior to add an essential layer of national pride to the law enforcement aesthetic. While the outside is strictly built for official police business, a short video released by the Italian State Police shows an interior cabin featuring black and tan leather, grounding the extreme performance machine with premium craftsmanship.The deployment of this 907-hp machine serves as the latest escalation in a highly successful, long-running operational partnership. Lamborghini and the Italian State Police officially began this specialized emergency transport initiative in 2004 with the introduction of its first dedicated model. Since the program originally started, the fleet has successfully transported over 200 organs, turning high-end automotive engineering into a tangible public health asset. Operational crews have fielded six different high-performance vehicles over the years, using them for intense medical missions and more than 1,500 road safety education events. This modernization of the two-decade initiative ensures that electrified performance provides the velocity required when every second counts.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week
Entertainment.text: SummaryPalace Skateboards has detailed its Fall 2026 Week 6 drop, spanning outerwear, denim, a trucker jacket and a graphic teeThe lineup foregrounds specific fabrics, from a 10 oz hooded canvas jacket to a Polartec-lined Legacy JacketPalace Skateboards has laid out the sixth weekly installment of its Fall 2026 season, a five-piece drop that puts its material choices front and center. The release runs from heavyweight canvas outerwear through technical fabrics and worked denim, giving each piece a distinct construction story rather than relying on graphics alone.The outerwear splits between raw material weight and technical performance. Anchoring the drop is a 10 oz Hooded Canvas Jacket, whose stated fabric weight signals a sturdy, structured build, offered in Black, Brown and Navy Blue. Running alongside it, the Polartec Legacy Jacket swaps canvas for a named technical fabric associated with warmth and insulation, arriving in Black and Racey Green for a more performance-minded option within the same release.Denim and the trucker bring the worked-fabric details. The Legacy P90 Jean comes in Black, Indigo and a Woodland Camo treatment, spanning a clean wash, a classic indigo and a patterned option in a single silhouette. The OM Distressed Trucker leans into finishing rather than fabric novelty, with a distressed treatment across Black, Realtree Edge and White that includes a licensed camo pattern among its colorways.The graphic piece keeps the range grounded in everyday staples. The Cat Face T-shirt rounds out the drop with the widest color spread of the five, offered in Black, White, Chalky Green and Grey Marl, giving the release an accessible entry point beneath the heavier outerwear and denim.Taken together, the five pieces read as a deliberately material-led drop, pairing raw canvas and technical fabric up top with camo-inflected denim and a distressed trucker below, each carried across several colorways to widen the options within a compact release.The Palace Skateboards Fall 2026 Week 6 drop launches Friday, September 11 at 11:00 a.m. BST across the UK, Europe and US, followed by Saturday, September 12 at 11:00 a.m. local time in Japan, China, Korea and Australia.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: A.PRESSE and Supreme Build a Fall 2026 Collection on Calfskin, Silk-Cotton Suiting and Hand-Applied Camo
Entertainment.text: SummarySupreme has partnered with Japanese brand A.PRESSE on a Fall 2026 collection spanning leather outerwear, tailoring, knitwear and accessoriesThe lineup leans on custom-developed fabrics, including a cotton-silk suit, a David & John Anderson Oxford shirt and hand-applied camo on the M-65 and Cargo PantThe pieces were produced by A.PRESSE across Japan, Portugal and the USA with custom fits built collaborativelySupreme and A.PRESSE have unveiled a Fall 2026 collection that channels the Japanese label's fabric-first, heritage-minded approach across a full run of apparel and accessories. The collaboration threads A.PRESSE's custom-developed materials and vintage finishing through leather jackets, tailoring, workwear staples and hardware, each piece cut to fits the two brands developed together.The materials do much of the talking here, in keeping with A.PRESSE's reputation. The label, founded by Kazuma Shigematsu in 2021, built its name on reinterpreting workwear, military and tailored archetypes through meticulously sourced fabrics and vintage finishing techniques, and the collaboration puts that sensibility front and center. Rather than leaning on graphics, the collection foregrounds construction and cloth as its main points of interest.The outerwear anchors the range in leather and military reference. A Leather Jacket arrives in two distinct hides, one in calfskin and one in cowhide, offering different weights and hands within the same silhouette. Alongside it, the M-65 and Cargo Pant both carry a hand-applied camo pattern, a labor-intensive finishing choice that ties the pieces to A.PRESSE's vintage-treatment approach while nodding to the military lineage that informs the brand.Tailoring and shirting extend the fabric story. The Suit is cut from a cotton-silk blend that balances structure with a softer drape, while the Shirt uses a David & John Anderson cotton pin Oxford, a nod to premium British-milled cloth. The Vintage Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt adds a cotton waffle thermal lining for texture and warmth, and a Tee brings in original photography by Ari Marcopoulos, folding an art-world collaborator into the otherwise material-led lineup.Accessories round the collection out and stretch it into hardware. A Camp Cap and a Cashmere Beanie cover headwear across seasons, while a 20-inch sterling silver Classic Key Chain gives the range a precious-metal endpoint. The full collection was produced by A.PRESSE in Japan, Portugal and the USA, with the custom fits across every piece developed jointly by the two brands, underscoring that the collaboration extends to pattern and cut rather than branding alone.A.PRESSE's profile continues to build beyond this release, with HBX having announced a dedicated space with the brand launching on September 10, a sign of the label's growing reach.The A.PRESSE x Supreme Fall 2026 collection releases September 10, followed by an Asia release on September 12.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The Nike First Sight Shadow Closes the Trilogy With Sculptural Slip-On Build in "Light Crimson/Metallic Silver"
Entertainment.text: Name: Nike First Sight Shadow “Light Crimson and Metallic Silver”Colorway: Light Crimson/Metallic SilverSKU: HQ2410-600MSRP: $145 USDRelease Date: September 15Where to Buy: NikeNike has unveiled the Women's First Sight Shadow in a "Light Crimson and Metallic Silver" colorway, positioning the model as the closing chapter of the brand's First Sight collection. The Shadow arrives as a slip-on silhouette that pulls its cues from early-2000s design while grounding itself in Nike's basketball lineage.Construction is where the Shadow makes its case. The model is built as a futuristic slip-on, doing away with traditional lacing in favor of an easy step-in entry, and it is topped by a sculptural upper that gives the shoe its molded, forward-leaning shape. That upper is the defining visual element, prioritizing a bold, contoured profile over conventional paneling.Underfoot, the traction is purpose-built rather than borrowed. Nike finishes the Shadow with a bespoke, court-inspired outsole pattern, tying the silhouette's grip back to the basketball reference points that inform the wider collection. It is a functional nod that keeps the design connected to performance roots even as the overall shape reads as street-focused.The design language traces directly to the early 2000s. The Shadow draws on the silhouettes of that era and filters them through Nike basketball DNA, translating a specific moment in the brand's hoops history into a contemporary, slip-on form. That lineage is what separates the model from a purely futuristic exercise, anchoring its forward-looking build in a recognizable design heritage.Within the First Sight lineup, the Shadow carries a specific role. Nike frames the collection as an effort to push athletic style into new territory, and the Shadow completes that three-model arc, presented as the piece that rounds out the trilogy. The "Light Crimson and Metallic Silver" treatment gives that closing entry a high-contrast finish to match its sculptural form.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Etro Leads the Birkenstock Boston and Gizeh With Paisley Outsoles and Pegaso Rivets
Entertainment.text: Name: Etro x Birkenstock Boston, Etro x Birkenstock GizehColorway: TBCSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: September 10Where to Buy: Birkenstock, EtroBirkenstock and Etro have released their collaborative footwear, opening with the Boston and the Gizeh as the first pairs in the partnership. The two styles graft Etro's decorative language onto Birkenstock's most recognizable silhouettes while leaving the brand's core footbed engineering intact.The ornamentation is where the collaboration concentrates its detailing. Both silhouettes are worked with a paisley motif and dense material treatments, then dressed with embroidered accents and long fringe for movement and texture. A Western-inspired buckle reshapes the closure hardware away from Birkenstock's standard fittings, while special rivets carry Etro's Pegaso emblem, embedding the house's identity into the functional hardware rather than only the surface.Underneath the decoration, the construction stays true to Birkenstock. Each style is built on the brand's anatomically shaped cork-latex footbed, the contoured base that defines how a Birkenstock sits and supports the foot. It anchors the collaboration's more expressive upper work to a familiar, function-first foundation, keeping the pairs recognizable as the Boston and Gizeh beneath the styling.The outsole is where both brands meet in a single component. Birkenstock's signature bone-pattern tread is retained for grip and identity, then overlaid with Etro's paisley motif, so the underfoot surface reads as a merger of the two design vocabularies. It turns a purely functional part of the shoe into another site for the co-branding.Positioned as the opening chapter of the tie-up, the Boston and Gizeh set the template for what the brands frame as a first drop, suggesting the collaboration is built to extend beyond these two styles.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Anbernic Reveals the RG DS Plus, a Dual-Screen Handheld Built for Nintendo DS Emulation Under $100 USD
Entertainment.text: SummaryAnbernic expands its retro gaming lineup with a larger dual-screen handheld engineered for authentic Nintendo DS emulationThe device transitions to a Linux operating system powered by the new NNDSS emulator featuring robust touch and microphone integrationHardware updates include an integrated capacitive stylus, a stepless dual alloy hinge and a strategic RAM adjustment to support GammaOSShenzhen-based hardware manufacturer Anbernic officially announced the Anbernic RG DS Plus, a dual-screen handheld gaming console inspired by the classic Nintendo DS. Arriving with a footprint larger than the original non-Plus model, this updated release is tailored for emulation. The device natively integrates a dual-screen setup alongside an integrated capacitive stylus and a built-in microphone to cater to the retro gaming community. This approach bridges a physical gap in portable emulation by addressing the hardware requirements necessary for legacy Nintendo DS titles.Front and center on the Anbernic RG DS Plus are its twin displays. Both screens measure 4.3 inches and deliver a 1024×768 resolution backed by 4x pixel-perfect scaling. The lower second display operates using a touch-based interface for the included stylus. Connecting these two panels is an upgraded dual alloy hinge. Built for a long lifespan, this hinge mechanism allows for stepless positioning to ensure optimal viewing angles. Physical inputs include four digital shoulder buttons and an analog stick. The handheld is also equipped with dual USB-C ports, dual microSD card slots, a headphone jack and front-facing speakers.A Linux operating system powers the handheld, shifting away from the Android OS used on its predecessor. This software foundation relies on a newly developed dual-screen emulator called NNDSS. The NNDSS emulator natively supports microphone input, allowing players to use the built-in mic for gameplay mechanics. Specialized software delivers screen swapping, an instant save feature and a real-time clock. Players can also customize visual output by cycling through 76 built-in shader options.Internal architecture makes trade-offs to balance community-driven software with affordability. The device is powered by the Rockchip RK3568 chipset, a processor unchanged from the previous version. The system features 1GB of RAM, representing a deliberate downgrade from the previous model's 3GB. This adjustment is the result of a collaboration with @TheGammaSqueeze to port GammaOS to the platform. To maintain the price point of the earlier model, Anbernic removed the built-in eMMC memory.Enthusiast-grade features arrive in a highly accessible tier. Anbernic offers the Anbernic RG DS Plus in three distinct color options: Metallic Blue, Matte Black and Coral Pink. While an official release date is not yet announced, the console will be priced below $100. Early adopters will have an introductory price of around $90 USD available during the first 72 hours of the launch.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Neil Druckmann Confirms Multiple New 'The Last of Us' Projects Are in Development at Naughty Dog
Entertainment.text: SummaryNeil Druckmann confirmed that Naughty Dog has stepped away from the creative direction of HBO's adaptation of "The Last of Us"The acclaimed studio maintains stewardship of the hit franchise with multiple undisclosed gaming projects actively in the worksDruckmann is currently focused on co-directing and co-writing a new title called "Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet"Speaking recently to the Washington Post, Neil Druckmann set the record straight on where Naughty Dog stands with the hit television adaptation of its flagship property. While the game director previously served as the co-creator and co-showrunner of the HBO series alongside Craig Mazin, Druckmann formally announced his departure from the television show in 2025. He confirmed that both he and the studio were uninvolved in shaping the creative direction for the upcoming season of The Last of Us, which is scheduled to return to screens in 2027.Stepping back from the television spotlight does not mean the studio is abandoning the property. Druckmann affirmed the developer's continued ownership of the franchise, stating that as the creator of the games, Naughty Dog remains the steward of the IP. Driving the point home to fans, Druckmann guaranteed the franchise's continuation by declaring that while this adaptation might end, the team is not done with the series. He teased that the studio currently has a couple projects in the works that he remains excited to discuss when the time is right.While those mystery titles develop in secrecy, the studio is pushing boundaries on its upcoming slate. Druckmann and Naughty Dog are currently deep into active development on a brand-new project titled Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. Bringing his focus back to the native gaming medium, Druckmann is serving a dual role by co-directing and co-writing the new title.This internal focus marks a pivot for the developer after Naughty Dog previously canceled a massive and highly anticipated multiplayer project set within the franchise universe. Druckmann had hinted that a third game in the franchise was in the works. Now, with a new console generation looming and the television show boosting popularity, the studio is positioned to capitalize on the renewed cultural demand for its signature prestige single-player entries.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Bad Bunny's Super Bowl Halftime Show Makes a Historic Seven Emmy Sweep
Entertainment.text: SummaryThe Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny took every category it was nominated for at Emmys Night 1, formerly the Creative Arts EmmysIts win for Outstanding Variety Special (Live) made it only the second halftime show ever to claim the top program prize and the first Spanish-language program to do soThe victory caps a landmark year that also saw Debí Tirar Más Fotos become the first Spanish-language album to win the GRAMMY for Album of the YearBad Bunny's Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show has become the most awarded Super Bowl performance in Emmy history, sweeping all seven categories it was nominated for at the 2026 Creative Emmy Awards. The wins hand the Puerto Rican superstar his first Emmy and cement a 13-minute set as one of the most decorated live productions of the season.The sweep was built on craft as much as star power. Alongside the top prize for Outstanding Variety Special (Live), the show collected trophies for directing, music direction, choreography, sound mixing, lighting design, technical direction and camerawork, a spread of wins that reads like a full accounting of everything that goes into staging a halftime show. Each category rewarded a different discipline behind the performance, which threaded Puerto Rican imagery and Latin music through guest turns from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin.The Outstanding Variety Special (Live) win carries the most weight historically. It marks only the second time a Super Bowl halftime show has taken the category's top program prize, following the 2022 performance that united Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Mary J. Blige, Eminem, Kendrick Lamar and 50 Cent. More significantly, it is the first Spanish-language program to win the award, a distinction that mirrors the barrier-breaking arc Bad Bunny has been on for the better part of a year.The Emmy arrives seven months after Debí Tirar Más Fotos (I Should Have Taken More Photos) became the first Spanish-language album to win the GRAMMY for Album of the Year, stacking two of the industry's highest honors within a single historic run. The through line is a body of work that has kept pushing Spanish-language art into spaces it had never occupied.The performance itself was framed by the message Bad Bunny delivered from the stage. "The only thing more powerful than hate is love," he said as he opened the show, a line that landed amid the noise surrounding his selection to headline. On Saturday night, Emmy voters offered a rejoinder of their own.The recognition didn’t stop at the Super Bowl though. The Saturday Night Live season opener that Bad Bunny hosted won Outstanding Makeup for a Variety, Nonfiction or Reality Program, giving a second production featuring the artist an Emmy on the same night and rounding out an evening that belonged, in almost every measurable way, to him.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Longevity & Anti-Aging.title: Aging rises, yet the double burden of illness remains
Longevity & Anti-Aging.text: Nature Aging, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43587-026-01218-8Ashwin and colleagues propose a statistical framing of the epidemiological transition that categorizes global diseases into four life-stages, identifying aging-related diseases as the dominant category. As aging-related diseases tend to cluster and span many years, health systems must pivot from treating disease to preserving health through investments in all life stages.
